project.name: Atlantic Auto and Shipping Services
project.one_liner: Website and tracking for a USA vehicle importer: import quotes, vehicle update requests, and team-managed tracking pages fed by the carrier.

intent.label: Product
intent.value: Lead-capture website with customer tracking pages and a small team admin

intent.label: Primary users
intent.value: Prospective importers, existing customers, and Atlantic staff

intent.label: Usage
intent.value: Customers occasionally on phones; staff daily

intent.label: Primary jobs
intent.value: Request a quote; request an update; check a vehicle's stage; staff keep stages current

intent.label: Platform
intent.value: Responsive web, mobile-first public site, desktop-first admin

decisions.title: Constraint
decisions.value: Prospects cannot start a USA import quote online, and existing customers have no clear way to ask where their vehicle is, so both land as ad hoc calls and WhatsApp messages that are slow to answer and easy to lose.
decisions.rationale: Restated from the brief's two primary buttons.

decisions.title: The bet
decisions.value: Customers will use simple online forms if they are quicker than calling; several weeks of build; watch quote requests per week and update requests that arrive with a VIN or reference.
decisions.rationale: Delegated by the owner.

decisions.title: Two primary actions
decisions.value: Every page leads to Request an Import Quote (primary) and Request a Vehicle Update (secondary).
decisions.rationale: Stated in the homepage copy.

decisions.title: USA import scope
decisions.value: The site is about importing vehicles from the USA, from point of sale through shipping. The mockup's general pickup/destination planner is dropped.
decisions.rationale: The copy replaces the mockup's generic shipping framing.

decisions.title: Site map
decisions.value: Home, How It Works, Request an Import Quote, Request a Vehicle Update, About Us, Contact, Privacy. One page per form so each can be linked from WhatsApp.
decisions.rationale: Replaced by PG-018 after the owner widened scope on 17 Nov 2026.

decisions.title: Import quote form
decisions.value: Short form: name, phone (WhatsApp), email optional, vehicle year/make/model, where it is in the USA (auction, dealer or private, with a listing link if any), destination, and notes. No payment on the site.
decisions.rationale: Enough to price a quote without scaring off a first-time importer.

decisions.title: Vehicle update request
decisions.value: Request form, not live tracking: name, phone, VIN or order reference, and question. The team replies by WhatsApp or phone. No customer login in v1.
decisions.rationale: Replaced by PG-020 after the owner widened scope on 17 Nov 2026.

decisions.title: Where submissions go
decisions.value: Each form sends a notification to the team's email, shows a reference number on the thank-you screen, and offers a 'Continue on WhatsApp' link with the details prefilled.
decisions.rationale: Matches the team's current WhatsApp habit while capturing every request.

decisions.title: How It Works journey
decisions.value: A plain step timeline: you buy (or we help you find) the vehicle, pickup in the USA, port and loading, ocean shipping, arrival and clearing, handover. Each step says what the customer hears from us.
decisions.rationale: Replaced by PG-019 after the owner widened scope on 17 Nov 2026.

decisions.title: Audience
decisions.value: First-time and repeat importers, mostly non-experts, visiting a few times around a purchase.
decisions.rationale: Occasional, novice users inferred from the service.

decisions.title: Mobile-first
decisions.value: Designed for phones first, with full parity on desktop. Sticky bottom bar on mobile with both actions.
decisions.rationale: Customers arrive from WhatsApp and social links on phones.

decisions.title: Slow-network tolerance
decisions.value: Lean pages: compressed responsive images, no heavy scripts, forms work with JavaScript off, clear retry on failure.
decisions.rationale: Mobile data and patchy connections are common for the audience.

decisions.title: Brand from the logo
decisions.value: Navy and teal from the supplied logo; light theme with navy hero and footer bands, as in the mockup.
decisions.rationale: Logo and mockup supplied.

decisions.title: Photography
decisions.value: The client supplies all landing page and hero images. Nothing is generated or taken from stock. Until a file arrives, its slot shows a plain navy or pale panel, never a placeholder photo, and no image ships without the client's file. Images are resized and compressed for mobile data at build. No car brand logos as decoration.
decisions.rationale: Replaced by PG-028 on 17 Nov 2026 (owner's new mockup).

decisions.title: Trust signals
decisions.value: Phone, WhatsApp, office location and email in the header, footer and Contact page (values supplied by the client, never placeholders at launch), plus real customer photos or testimonials once supplied. No invented reviews or numbers.
decisions.rationale: Main hesitation is trusting an importer with money and a car.

decisions.title: WCAG 2.2 AA baseline
decisions.value: Keyboard operable, visible focus, 4.5:1 text contrast, labelled form fields with inline errors, 44px touch targets.
decisions.rationale: Studio baseline.

decisions.title: Forms style
decisions.value: Large labelled inputs, custom select chevron in teal (studio rule), one column on mobile, progress-free single page.
decisions.rationale: Short forms for novice users.

decisions.title: Site map (v2)
decisions.value: Public: Home, Cars for Sale, car detail pages, Services, How It Works, Request an Import Quote, Request a Vehicle Update, About Us, Contact, Privacy. Staff: sign-in, shipments list, shipment detail.
decisions.rationale: Adds services, tracking and the team area the owner asked for.

decisions.title: Full-service scope
decisions.value: Atlantic handles sourcing, purchase, pickup, shipping, clearance and delivery. Services page and How It Works present these six steps, and customers can ask for any or all of them in the quote form.
decisions.rationale: Stated by the owner.

decisions.title: Request a Vehicle Update form
decisions.value: Form: name, phone (WhatsApp), VIN or tracking reference, question. If the vehicle has a tracking page, the thank-you screen links to it; the team still replies by WhatsApp or phone.
decisions.rationale: Stated by the owner.

decisions.title: Team-managed tracking page
decisions.value: Each vehicle has a tracking page showing its stage on a six-step timeline (Sourcing, Purchased, Picked up, Shipped, Clearing, Delivered) with dates, a short team note and optional photos. Staff set the stage; the carrier feed fills in vessel, ETA and container events while shipped.
decisions.rationale: Replaced by PG-030 on 18 Nov 2026 (client: tracking is for the company, not customers, for now).

decisions.title: How customers open their tracking page
decisions.value: Two ways: a private link the team sends on WhatsApp, or the Track Your Vehicle page with tracking reference plus last 4 digits of the phone on file. No customer accounts. VIN alone never opens a page.
decisions.rationale: Replaced by PG-030 on 18 Nov 2026 (client: tracking is for the company, not customers, for now).

decisions.title: Team admin area
decisions.value: Staff sign in to a simple admin: list of shipments with stage filters, create a shipment from a quote, change stage, add notes and photos, enter carrier booking or container number, see incoming quote and update requests. This is where the company tracks every vehicle. Desktop-first, works on a phone for quick stage changes.
decisions.rationale: Client: tracking is mainly for the company; the admin is the tracking tool.

decisions.title: Carrier integration
decisions.value: Pull vessel name, ETA and container milestones automatically from the carrier (or a container-tracking service covering it) using the booking, bill of lading or container number, shown to staff in the admin. Staff can always override. Which carriers and which API are chosen at build after a lookup, not guessed.
decisions.rationale: Owner asked for a carrier integration; carriers are not yet named.

decisions.title: Who receives enquiries
decisions.rationale: Owner: one shared inbox with category tabs; Car Enquiries added with car sales (18 Nov 2026).
decisions.value: One shared inbox with category tabs: All, Import Quotes, Vehicle Updates and Car Enquiries, each with a count of new items. Every type also emails the same company address with its category at the start of the subject ([Import Quote], [Vehicle Update], [Car Enquiry]) so mail filters can sort them.

decisions.title: Ghanaian company, Ghana market
decisions.value: Atlantic is a Ghanaian company importing vehicles from the USA into Ghana. Copy speaks to Ghanaian buyers, arrival and clearance are at Tema port, phone numbers use +233 format, WhatsApp is the main contact channel, and photography shows Ghanaian people and Tema rather than generic foreign ports.
decisions.rationale: Stated by the owner.

decisions.title: Landing page sections
decisions.value: 1 Hero (supplied copy, both buttons). 2 Track Your Vehicle quick box. 3 Services: the six steps as cards. 4 How it works: USA lot to your door in Ghana timeline. 5 Why Atlantic: Ghanaian team, one contact throughout, updates at every stage, paperwork handled (no invented figures). 6 What we import: cars, SUVs, pickups and trucks from auctions, dealers and private sellers. 7 What your cost is made of: purchase, US towing, ocean freight, Tema duty and clearance, delivery (explained, no rates). 8 Clearing at Tema: what we handle and documents you need. 9 Recent deliveries and testimonials (shown only once real ones are supplied). 10 FAQ. 11 About Us (supplied copy). 12 Closing call to action with phone, WhatsApp, office and email.
decisions.rationale: Replaced by PG-029 on 17 Nov 2026 (owner's new mockup).

decisions.title: Images and car brand logos
decisions.value: The client supplies all landing page and hero photos (no stock, nothing generated); empty slots show a pale panel with an icon. 'What we import' shows the real Toyota, Honda, Ford, Mercedes-Benz and Isuzu logos with example models (Camry, CR-V, Ranger, Sprinter, NPR), using official files recorded in brand/LOGOS.md. The footer uses a white version of the Atlantic logo.
decisions.rationale: Owner, 17 Nov 2026: 'add the real logo and car brands', overriding the earlier no-brand-logos rule for this site.

decisions.title: Landing page layout (owner mockup)
decisions.value: Follows the owner's 17 Nov mockup without the customer track bar: hero, six photo service cards, featured cars for sale (PG-031), six-stage icon stepper ('tracked by our team'), four 'why Atlantic' points, five vehicle-type cards with brand logos plus a sources strip, five cost parts, Tema section, testimonials hidden until real, then FAQ, About Us (CSS shipment-progress illustration) and Contact.
decisions.rationale: Owner mockup, adjusted on 18 Nov 2026 when customer tracking was hidden.

decisions.title: Tracking is for the team (customer tracking hidden)
decisions.value: The company tracks every vehicle in the staff admin (stages, notes, photos, carrier data). Customer tracking pages, private links and the reference lookup are switched off by the features.customer_tracking setting and every public link to them is hidden; the code stays so it can be switched on later. Customers get updates through Request a Vehicle Update, WhatsApp or phone.
decisions.rationale: Client, 18 Nov 2026: the three main things are selling cars, shipping and tracking, but tracking is mainly for the company, not customers; hide customer tracking for now.

decisions.title: Cars for Sale pages
decisions.value: New 'Cars for Sale' menu item. /cars lists published cars as photo cards (photo, year, make, model, price, status badge, key specs) with filters for availability and body type. /cars/{reference} is the detail page: photo gallery, price, status, specs (year, make, model, body type, mileage, transmission, fuel, engine, colour, where the car is now: in the USA, in transit or in Ghana), description, and buttons for 'I'm interested' and WhatsApp. The home page gets a 'Featured cars for sale' section directly after the service cards: up to six available cars that staff marked as featured (newest available cars if none are featured), with a 'See all cars' link; hidden when no car is published.
decisions.rationale: Owner: product sale section with detail pages and amounts; selling cars is one of the three main things the business does. Owner, 18 Nov 2026: featured cars for sale on the landing page after the services cards.

decisions.title: Prices and availability
decisions.value: Each car has a price amount and currency (GHS by default, USD allowed per car) or 'Price on request'. Status is Available, Reserved or Sold, shown as a badge. Sold and Reserved cars stay listed with their badge and no enquiry button until staff hide them. Prices are entered by staff; the site never calculates or estimates prices.
decisions.rationale: Owner: amounts plus available or sold out. Reserved covers a deposit in progress. GHS is the studio's currency of record; USD allowed for cars priced in dollars.

decisions.title: Car management in the admin
decisions.value: New 'Cars' section in the staff admin: list with status and visibility filters; add and edit a car (all fields above); upload up to 12 photos and choose the main one; change status in one click; mark a car as Featured for the home page; Publish or Hide (hidden cars disappear from the site immediately but keep their data); delete is Admin only with typed confirmation. Every change is in the audit log.
decisions.rationale: Owner: update available or sold out, and the ability to hide in the admin.

decisions.title: Car enquiries
decisions.value: 'I'm interested' on an available car opens a short form (name, phone or WhatsApp, optional message) with the same spam protection as the other forms. It lands in the inbox under Car Enquiries, linked to the car, emails the shared inbox as [Car Enquiry], and the thank-you screen offers 'Continue on WhatsApp' with the car's reference.
decisions.rationale: Turns a listing into a lead the same way as quotes and updates.

directions.name: Harbour Trust
directions.tagline: The mockup, sharpened around the two actions.
directions.fit: Keeps what you already liked in the mockup (navy hero, teal buttons, photo cards) and refocuses it on USA imports and the two requests. Lowest risk and fastest to build.
directions.tradeoffs: Familiar shipping-company look; less distinctive than a custom concept.

foundation.Theme: Light with navy hero and footer bands
foundation.Navigation: Top bar, sticky mobile action bar
foundation.Primary interaction: Two calls to action, short forms, stage timeline

directions.name: Two Doors
directions.tagline: Utility first: pick your door, get it done.
directions.fit: The homepage is two big panels, 'I want to import a vehicle' and 'I already have a vehicle with you'. Lightest pages, best on slow phones.
directions.tradeoffs: Less atmosphere and storytelling; relies on copy and trust signals more than photography.
directions.why_not: Plainer than the mockup the client already saw; trust has to come from words alone.

directions.name: The Crossing
directions.tagline: Tell the journey from US lot to home port.
directions.fit: A scrolling story of the vehicle's journey with large photography and a step timeline. Strongest emotional pull and best answers 'where is my car now'.
directions.tradeoffs: Heavier pages and more imagery to produce; slower on mobile data; more build time.
directions.why_not: Heaviest on slow phone connections and needs the most imagery and build time for a site whose job is two short forms.

risks.text: Forms collect names, phones and VINs: personal data that needs spam protection and safe handling (security gate).
No real photos, testimonials or business details supplied yet; trust content may launch thin.
Carrier APIs vary: some carriers have none, and tracking services may charge. Costs and coverage must be looked up before build.
Tracking pages and the admin hold customer, vehicle and payment-stage data; access control is the main job of the security gate.
Tracking pages go stale if staff do not update stages; the admin must make updates take seconds.
Customers may expect live GPS; copy must say stages are updated by the team and the carrier.
Ghana duty and clearance rules change; the clearance section must avoid figures and link to the team for current costs.

assumptions.text: The team handles requests by email and WhatsApp; no CRM integration in v1.
No online payment in v1; purchase payments are handled offline.
Phone, WhatsApp, office address and email will be supplied by the client before launch.
Constraint has no measured evidence yet; it is based on the owner's description.
No prices, duty rates or transit times are published until the client supplies them; cost and clearance sections explain components only.
The shared inbox address will be supplied with the other contact details before launch.
Client-supplied images arrive before launch, with the right to use them; the hero needs at least one wide image (about 2400px) and a portrait crop for phones.

gate.approval_quote: Approve both (answering: Approve the Project Gate changes and security baseline 0.2.0?)

constraint.statement: Prospects cannot start a USA import quote online, and existing customers have no clear way to ask where their vehicle is, so both land as ad hoc calls and WhatsApp messages that are slow to answer and easy to lose.
constraint.evidence: Owner's description of current enquiries (see AS-07).

forces.push: Importing a car from the USA feels opaque: unclear steps, costs and where the car is right now.
forces.pull: A quick import quote request and a simple way to ask for a vehicle update.
forces.anxiety: Trusting an importer with an expensive vehicle and a large payment, and not hearing anything once it ships.
forces.habit: Calling or WhatsApping the team, or an agent they know, and waiting for a reply.

bet.belief: customers will use simple online forms if they are quicker than calling
bet.expected_outcome: more import quote requests captured and vehicle update requests that arrive complete and get answered faster
bet.leading_indicator: quote requests per week, and share of update requests with a VIN or reference

outcomes: More import quote requests are captured
Vehicle update requests arrive complete and are answered faster
